requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.index.chapter`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request implementation source.

**Directive form (standalone, empty body, opening and closing fences)**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` accepts a `::::` fence with a matching `::::` close.
- The same test accepts a longer closing fence (`::::` opened, `:::::` closed).
- It rejects a closing fence shorter than the opening one.
- It rejects a missing close.
- It rejects a non-empty body.
- It ignores markers in code fences and in other directives.
- It ignores `::{...}` with only two colons.
- It ignores an inline, non-standalone `Inline :::{...}`.
- It checks that the matched range is exactly the standalone directive.

**At most one directive per book**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two markers in separate chapters.
- It also covers two markers in one chapter.
- Both cases must fail with an error containing "only one".

**Index lists all definitions and links each to its detail page**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` checks a row for each of 5 requirements. Each row has a link to `requirements-index/requirements.core.<name>.html` and the expected evidence state.
- The same test checks that table columns are aligned.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers a mix of requirements and examples, and a nested child chapter. It checks the "(requirement)" and "(example)" markers and the detail pages for all four definitions in order.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` covers definitions spread over several chapters. It checks the detail page names and their order.
- Together these tests also cover the detail-page links, whose content is owned by `requirements.index.detail_pages`.

**Directive replaced by the table when present**
- The index test in `src/index.rs` asserts that the `{requirements-index}` text is gone and the table is present in the same chapter.
- The explicit-index test in `src/lib.rs` asserts `book.items.len() == 3`. So the explicit index keeps its placement and no default chapter is appended.

**Default chapter when there is no directive**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers the default chapter with definitions.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers a book with no definitions, with and without prose. In the prose case the only marker is inside a code block.
- Both tests assert the name, the path `requirements-index.md`, the missing `source_path`, no parent names, and the section number.
- The detailed default behaviour belongs to `requirements.index.chapter.default`, which these tests also reference.

I found no scenario the requirement names that is left untested, and no acknowledged gaps apply.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
